Knowing which app was opened last, for the “Lock this app” tile. While BioKey has nothing to watch (protection paused or no app locked), it looks only when the tile is shown or tapped, and no further back than 6 hours.

A log of BioKey’s own lock decisions about your locked apps, and of pauses, Security activity, waits after wrong passphrases and backups as they happen.\nIt stays on this phone for 3 days, at most 500 entries. If the phone restarts and can’t get the time from the network, the last 500 are kept until it can.\nYou can turn off “Diagnostic log” in BioKey’s settings.
Security activity, which records:
Times protection was off, including BioKey being reset (its storage cleared)
Faces or fingerprints added or removed
Times the phone had no screen lock
Unlocks let through on Android’s word alone, when the phone’s hardware couldn’t prove the match
Your passphrase being set, changed or removed
A face or fingerprint that couldn’t be used, so your screen lock was allowed
Failed unlocks, if you turn on “Failed unlock alerts”

Security activity also records changes made after BioKey was opened with your screen lock, or within a day of a face or fingerprint change or a reset, naming the app or profile changed. Reminders stopped within that day, and the diagnostic log shared at those times, are recorded too.

Each Security activity record is kept until you’ve seen it (at least a day for a face or fingerprint change or a reset), and for 7 days after it happened. At most 500 unseen failed unlocks and 500 other unseen records are kept: past that, the oldest and the newest stay and those in between go, though a face or fingerprint change or a reset is always kept. Once seen, at most 50 failed unlocks and 20 other records are kept, besides face or fingerprint changes and resets.
Which of your locked apps Android’s own App lock was seen locking too, for 30 days
For each app you’ve locked, a code worked out from the certificates it’s signed with

If you uninstall a locked app, that code is kept with its package name (the ID Android knows it by, such as com.example.bank) and its profile for 30 days. Reinstalled from the same developer, it’s locked again; from anyone else, BioKey offers to lock it.
BioKey never sends anything it sees or keeps off this phone: it has no internet access. Only a diagnostic log you share or a backup you save leaves it.
BioKey never reads what you type, your messages or anything in other apps beyond what’s listed above
